title: Interarch Building Solutions Ltd - 544232 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Interarch Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR460 crores, EBITDA up 24.6% to INR39 crores, PAT flat at INR28 crores; order book INR1,864 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 20.7% YoY to INR460 crores and EBITDA grew 24.6% to INR39 crores, with margin stable at 8.6%. PAT was flat at INR28 crores as other income fell because IPO cash was spent on capex. Management raised FY27 revenue to INR2,700 crores for FY28 (from INR2,500 crores) and kept FY27 guidance at INR2,150-2,200 crores. Order book stood at INR1,864 crores as of 31 July 2026, and a QIP was approved at INR250 crores, up from INR100 crores earlier.

financial_highlights.change: up ~9% QoQ per analyst; management said increased over last 3 months
positive; prior-year Q1 had negative operating cash flow

segments.name: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB)
segments.commentary: Core business; capacity about 221,000 tonnes after Kheda (Gujarat) Phase 1 inauguration; FY26 sales 162,000 tonnes (~80% of installed, ~88% of utilisable capacity). Gujarat plant started 9 July 2026; Phase 2 expected by October 2026.

segments.name: Heavy structures (Andhra Pradesh, Pantnagar Kichha line)
segments.commentary: Trial production started; commercial production expected around end-August/early-September 2026. Phase 2 targeted by March 2027 and Phase 3 by December 2027, for a total of about 75,000-80,000 tonnes. Management expects about INR100-150 crores of FY27 revenue from heavy structures.

segments.name: Buildings segment (multi-storey, data centres, hotels)
segments.commentary: Around 10% of Q1 revenue, versus about 0-2% previously, including a data centre order for RailTel in Noida. Management said about 35% of order book comes from new-age industries and new segments.

segments.name: Export / open web steel joist JV (Canada)
segments.commentary: JV with a Canadian partner (ER Steel) for a 15,000-tonne plant; first phase 4,000-5,000 tonnes (~$7.5m, ~INR70-75 crores) with ~20% EBITDA margin targeted. Production expected by July-end 2027. Management targets exports at about 10% of turnover in the short to medium term (1-2 years).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance kept at INR2,150-2,200 crores; management said it is well on track and may beat projections, but will revisit in about 3-4 months.
FY28 revenue projection raised to INR2,700 crores from INR2,500 crores, including about INR200 crores from heavy structures.
EBITDA and PBT targets for FY27 unchanged; FY28 EBITDA margin aim of 9.5-10%.
Quarterly run-rate of about INR600 crores targeted for the next 3-4 quarters, with quarters varying (e.g. INR550-620 crores); about INR1,700 crores needed in the next 9 months.
FY27 volume growth around 18%, to roughly 190,000 tonnes.
Capex planned at about INR129 crores in FY27 and INR133 crores in FY28 (roughly INR250 crores over two years, per management).
Margin expansion expected mainly in FY28 rather than immediately, as new plants carry upfront costs.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 221,000 tonnes per year including Kheda Phase 1; Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant) started 9 July 2026, Phase 2 by October 2026.
Heavy structure plant in Andhra Pradesh: trial production underway, commercial production around end-August/early-September 2026; Phase 2 by March 2027; Phase 3 by December 2027.

QIP approved at INR250 crores (earlier INR100 crores approved about six months ago), with use of funds about INR140-150 crores for heavy structure Phases 2-3, INR50-60 crores for Gujarat Plant 2, and INR50-60 crores for the Canadian open web joist export unit. Timing not decided; may be within the next 4 months.
About INR240 crores of capex spent from April 2024 to date, versus INR180 crores raised in the IPO.
PEB new plants are set up only once existing plants reach 80-90% utilisation; heavy structure utilisation expected to be clearer by March 2027.
demand_pricing: Order book INR1,864 crores as of 31 July 2026, including a INR165 crore order from a major energy company in Vadodara; management said orders are booked on a basis of about INR600 crores per quarter.
Order mix: about 35% from new-age industries and new segments (EV, semiconductor, lithium battery, data centres, multi-storey buildings).
Management said execution was affected by site clearances and monsoon in Q1 and Q2; slower first half is seasonal.

Some recent energy-sector orders have 15-16 month execution periods (HVDC valve halls, variable price contracts), against 8-12 months for normal orders, due to longer site clearances (about 6 months).
Cost pressures cited: steel prices and shortages (linked to the Iran war), freight, labour and site manpower; erection prices have risen.
Management said competition is intensifying but pie is expanding; price pressure exists, but management is focused on profitability over revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue (INR460 crores) lower than Q3/Q4 last year and even Q2, given the INR600 crore quarterly run-rate target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the seasonal Q1/Q2 dip to site clearances and monsoon; it said order book and capacity are in place and the run-rate will vary (e.g. INR550-620 crores), needing about INR1,700 crores over the next 9 months. The Andhra phase 2 (about 20,000 tonnes) came online in September 2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned use of the INR250 crore QIP, and why was it raised from INR100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Heavy structure Phases 2-3 in Andhra about INR140-150 crores, Gujarat Plant 2 INR50-60 crores, and the Canadian open web joist export unit INR50-60 crores. Management said the expansion is being sped up, and the IPO raised about INR180 crores against about INR240 crores of capex spent since April 2024.

qa_highlights.question: Details on the ER Steel Canada JV: rationale, and revenue potential over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Partner handles sales, engineering and customers in North America; Interarch handles manufacturing. The 15,000-tonne plant could yield about $20-23 million at full capacity over 2-3 years. Phase 1 is 4,000-5,000 tonnes (about $7.5m, INR70-75 crores) at about 20% EBITDA, with production targeted by July-end 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sales were 162,000 tonnes against 200,000 tonnes capacity (about 80%, about 88% of utilisable capacity). Capacity is now about 221,000 tonnes and Q1 volume was 38,499 tonnes (about 80% of 50,000 tonnes quarterly capacity). Margin gains are expected mainly in FY28, not immediately, as new plants carry upfront costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise QIP when cash generation appears sufficient, and what capex is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited working capital needs for larger orders and a desire to raise funds once for the next two years. Capex is about INR129 crores in FY27 and INR133 crores in FY28. Timing is undecided and could fall within about 4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are some energy-sector orders on 15-16 month execution periods, and what is the export contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: The orders are for HVDC valve halls from EPC contractors on variable-price terms, and site clearances take about 6 months versus 2-3 months normally. Q1 exports were about INR10-12 crores of INR460 crores, and management targets about 10% of turnover from exports in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was finance cost up sharply, and what is the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has no debt. Finance cost rose because interest income fell as IPO cash was spent on capex, and a one-time bank processing fee was paid on enhanced non-fund-based limits. Non-fund limit utilisation was 82% versus 64% a year earlier.

risks_watch: Quarterly revenue lumpiness: management guides to about INR600 crores per quarter for the next 3-4 quarters, needing about INR1,700 crores in 9 months; Q1 was INR460 crores, so the H1 ramp is a key test.
Margin pressure from steel prices and shortages (linked to the Iran war), freight, labour and erection prices; management expects margin gains mainly in FY28 and EBITDA margin was 8.6%.

Execution risk on new capacity: Gujarat Phase 2 by October 2026, heavy structure commercial production around end-August/early-September 2026, and utilisation of heavy structures unclear until about March 2027.
Heavy structure order pipeline is still early; management is taking a cautious 5-6 month approach and the INR200 crore FY28 uplift depends on it.
Other income falling as IPO cash is spent on capex; PAT flat at INR28 crores, and finance cost up; watch how QIP proceeds (INR250 crores, timing undecided) affect treasury income and capex.
Competitive intensity and price pressure; management says competition is intensifying but the pie is growing, and it is prioritising profitability over revenue growth.
Revenue guidance kept at INR2,150-2,200 crores despite a 20.7% Q1 rise; management may revisit in 3-4 months, so watch for a guidance upgrade or a revision at the next call.
key_quotes: So we are well on track for our projections.
We want to revise our projections for '27 -'28 to INR2,700 crores from INR2,500 crores.

But I'm not very sure that it will show immediate results this year because we have to also, whenever we open new plants and new areas like we have done, Gujarat and heavy structure, a lot of expense goes into that in advance of actually the sale happening.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, order book and the expansion plan, but cautious on near-term revenue and guidance, repeatedly saying it would not revise FY27 guidance until more data arrives. It was evasive on the specific quarterly revenue shortfall and on margin timing, attributing both to seasonality and new-plant costs.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance held at INR2,150-2,200 crores (about 20% growth on the midpoint) and FY28 raised to INR2,700 crores; backed by the INR1,864 crore order book and heavy structures capacity starting around Aug-Sep 2026, though the new-plant schedule and the QIP timing are not firm.
